caption:
The medicine of women is oxytocin.

And no, not the simplified version you were taught about “the love hormone.” That is the reductionist version of something much deeper.

Oxytocin is one of the primary neurochemicals involved in female nervous system regulation. 

Women also appear more sensitive to oxytocin because estrogen increases oxytocin receptor activity. This means female physiology is deeply organized around connection and relational safety.

And when we begin to understand oxytocin, we begin to understand something profound about women and the modern world.

For thousands of years, belonging meant survival for women. A woman disconnected from her community was vulnerable. Female physiology evolved around co-regulation. Around rhythm, connection, touch, women, land, ritual and belonging.

But somewhere along the way, something shifted.

Modern systems quietly learned that when belonging creates safety and safety creates regulation, women become easier to organize and control around the fear of losing belonging.

Because when approval creates safety in the body, approval can become addictive.

Many women learned very early that belonging mattered more than authenticity. 

That being loved meant being agreeable. Easy. Selfless. Beautiful. Desirable. Good.

And slowly, women began abandoning themselves.

This is where self abandonment quietly becomes physiology.

One of the deepest ways this shaped women is through the belief that regulation lives outside of us. That we cannot truly feel safe without being chosen, without a relationship, without romantic love, without touch from men or without laying in someone else’s arms.

But women were never designed to regulate primarily through men.

Romantic connection was never meant to become the sole source of female nervous system regulation.

Women have always regulated through many forms of connection.

This is why women gathered. Why they sang together, cooked together, bled together, raised children together and lived close to the land.

Because women were never meant to carry regulation alone or outsource it entirely to one person.

author: Dr. Gabrielle Naomi
transcript: Women were never supposed to regulate through men, and a society built around male physiology quietly made sure that women forgot that. Because once you understand female biology, you realize that modern life depends on dysregulated women. Women do not regulate primarily through achievement, conquest, productivity, or dopamine. Women regulate through oxytocin. And before we all say, oh yeah, that's the love hormone. That's the simplified version, the patriarchal version. Oxytocin is female regulation. It influences whether a woman feels safe enough to access her own intuition, sexuality, fertility, her boundaries, and her deep inner knowing. A deeply regulated woman is very difficult to manipulate. Because when a woman feels safe inside of herself, she stops abandoning herself to belong. She stops outsourcing her authority. She stops betraying herself to be loved. So what happens in a structure that disconnects women from themselves and hijacks oxytocin? Women begin searching for regulation outside of themselves in approval, in beauty standards, in over giving, in relationships, in endless self-improvement, and even spirituality. Always searching for something to make the body finally feel safe. Because belonging produces oxytocin, and when that's threatened, many women will abandon themselves before risking abandonment from the group. This is a biological female trait because oxytocin is our medicine. And yes, women were designed to regulate through connection. But that's not only romantic connection to men. Women regulate through connection to themselves, to other women, to the body, to nature, to rhythm, to cycles, to the earth. This is why women always gathered, why rhythm mattered, why women lived closer to the land, and why disconnection from all of this makes women so sick. The real revolution is not chasing highs. It's not getting in power. It's not empowerment culture. The real revolution is women connecting so deeply to themselves and nature that nothing outside of themselves can control who they are.
title: Oxytocin: The Real Medicine of Women
one_liner: Women regulate through oxytocin and relational connection, not achievement — and modern life exploits this biology.
key_points: Oxytocin governs female nervous system regulation, not just romantic bonding; estrogen amplifies oxytocin receptor sensitivity
A regulated woman is harder to manipulate — self-abandonment often begins as a biological survival response to belonging threats
Modern systems hijack oxytocin by tying safety to approval, driving women toward people-pleasing, beauty standards, and over-giving
True female regulation comes from connection to self, other women, body, nature, and rhythm — not primarily from men
